\begin{theorem}[Genus-\texorpdfstring{$0$}{0} amplitudes from bar complex;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]\label{thm:genus0-amplitude-bar}
\index{string amplitude!bar complex}
Let $\cA$ be a chiral algebra on $\mathbb{P}^1$, and let
$\omega_1, \ldots, \omega_n$ be cocycles in
$\bar{B}^1(\cA)$.  Then the genus-$0$ string amplitude
\[
\mathcal{A}_0(\omega_1, \ldots, \omega_n)
\;=\;
\int_{\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}}
  \omega_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge \omega_n
\]
equals the bar complex Euler characteristic
$\chi(\bar{B}^n_0(\cA))$, where $\bar{B}^n_0$ denotes the
genus-$0$ component of the degree-$n$ bar complex.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Both sides compute the same configuration space integral.
The bar complex is realized on
$\overline{C}_n(\mathbb{P}^1) = \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n+1}$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-cobar-isomorphism-main}),
with the bar differential given by residues of the FM propagator
$\omega_{ij} = d\log(z_i - z_j)$ along collision divisors.
The string amplitude $\mathcal{A}_0$ inserts vertex operators
at marked points and integrates the resulting form over the
compactification; this is precisely the definition of the bar
complex pairing.  The Euler characteristic
$\chi(\bar{B}^n_0) = \sum_k (-1)^k \dim H^k(\bar{B}^n_0)$
equals the integral by the Gauss--Bonnet--Chern theorem on
$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ applied to the logarithmic
de~Rham complex: the logarithmic forms $\eta_{ij}$ provide
a resolution of the constant sheaf on
$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and integration of the
top-degree component is the Euler characteristic.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Anomaly duality from complementarity}

\begin{corollary}[Anomaly duality for Kac--Moody pairs;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{cor:anomaly-duality-km}
\index{anomaly cancellation!Kac--Moody duality}
\index{Feigin--Frenkel duality!anomaly interpretation}
Let $\widehat{\fg}_k$ be an affine Kac--Moody algebra at generic
level $k$, with Feigin--Frenkel dual
$\widehat{\fg}_{k'} = \widehat{\fg}_{-k-2h^\vee}$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item \emph{Bar cohomology = semi-infinite cohomology.}
If the native bar--semi-infinite chain comparison is supplied,
the bar cohomology computations of Part~\textup{II} transport to
semi-infinite cohomology.  The generic-rank statement of
Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-cohomology-level-independence} does not compute a
Hilbert series or construct that comparison.  Under the chain-comparison
hypothesis, the dimension equality is
\[
\dim H^n(\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\widehat{\fg}_k))
= \dim H^{\infty/2+n}(\widehat{\fg}_k, V_k).
\]

\item \emph{Curvature = conformal anomaly.}
The genus-$1$ curvature coefficient
$\kappa(\widehat{\fg}_k) = (k+h^\vee)\dim\fg/(2h^\vee)$
\textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:genus-universality}(i))} equals
the semi-infinite anomaly coefficient.  The duality
$\kappa + \kappa' = 0$ of
Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:genus-universality}(ii)} is the
anomaly cancellation for the Feigin--Frenkel pair: the
conformal anomalies of $\widehat{\fg}_k$ and
$\widehat{\fg}_{-k-2h^\vee}$ cancel.

\item \emph{Complementarity = anomaly duality.}
The quantum complementarity theorem
\textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:quantum-complementarity-main})}
applied to the Koszul pair
$(\widehat{\fg}_k, \widehat{\fg}_{-k-2h^\vee})$ gives:
\[
Q_g(\widehat{\fg}_k) \oplus Q_g(\widehat{\fg}_{-k-2h^\vee})
= H^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g,\, Z(\widehat{\fg}_k)).
\]
Via the bar--semi-infinite identification, the left side is a
direct sum of semi-infinite cohomology spaces on
$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$: the genus-$g$ quantum corrections
of the WZW model at level~$k$ and its Feigin--Frenkel dual sum to
the full moduli space cohomology.  This is the mathematical
content of anomaly cancellation for Kac--Moody pairs at all genera.

\item \emph{Universal MC duality.}
The universal Maurer--Cartan classes satisfy
$\Theta_{\widehat{\fg}_k} + \Theta_{\widehat{\fg}_{-k-2h^\vee}}
= 0$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit-theta}), since
$\kappa(\widehat{\fg}_k) + \kappa(\widehat{\fg}_{-k-2h^\vee}) = 0$
by Theorem~\ref{thm:genus-universality}(ii).
This is the chain-level mechanism underlying~(c):
the Verdier involution exchanges
$\Theta_{\widehat{\fg}_k}$ and $-\Theta_{\widehat{\fg}_{k'}}$,
producing the Lagrangian splitting of
Theorem~\ref{thm:quantum-complementarity-main}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Part~(a) is the cohomology-level consequence of
Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km}.  Part~(b): the
curvature $m_0 = \kappa \cdot \mathbf{1}$ in the bar complex
corresponds, under the quasi-isomorphism~$\Psi$, to the
semi-infinite anomaly (the failure of the naive CE differential
to square to zero, corrected by the semi-infinite charge).
The genus universality theorem identifies this with the
conformal anomaly coefficient.  The duality $\kappa + \kappa' = 0$
follows from the Feigin--Frenkel level shift and the formula
$\kappa = (k+h^\vee)\dim\fg/(2h^\vee)$: replacing $k$ by
$-k - 2h^\vee$ negates~$\kappa$.
Part~(c): combine the bar--semi-infinite identification with
Theorem~\ref{thm:quantum-complementarity-main}.  The genus-$g$
obstruction space $Q_g(\widehat{\fg}_k)$ is the associated
graded of $H^*(\barB^{(g)}(\widehat{\fg}_k))$, which by
Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km} is the genus-$g$
semi-infinite cohomology.  The complementarity sum equals
$H^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g, Z(\widehat{\fg}_k))$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:quantum-complementarity-main}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The Master Table, revisited]
\label{rem:master-table-brst}
\index{master table of invariants!BRST interpretation}
Via Corollary~\ref{cor:anomaly-duality-km}, every entry in the Master Table (Table~\ref{tab:master-invariants}) is a semi-infinite anomaly coefficient: $\kappa$ is the semi-infinite anomaly, $c + c' = 2\dim\fg$ the total Feigin--Frenkel anomaly, and $F_g$ the genus-$g$ WZW free energy.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Extension to $\mathcal{W}$-algebras via Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction}

\begin{theorem}[Bar complex = semi-infinite complex for \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{W}$}{W}-algebras;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w}
\index{semi-infinite cohomology!W-algebra identification}
\index{Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction!semi-infinite cohomology}
Let $\mathcal{W}^k(\fg, f_{\mathrm{prin}})$ be the principal
W-algebra at level $k \neq -h^\vee$.  There is a quasi-isomorphism:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bar-semi-infinite-w}
\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg))
\;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\;
C^{\infty/2+\bullet}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg),\, M_k)
\end{equation}
where $M_k$ is the vacuum module for $\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)$ and the
right side is the semi-infinite complex defined with respect to the
conformal weight grading.  In particular:
\[
H^*(\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)))
\;\cong\;
H^{\infty/2+*}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg),\, M_k).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The W-algebra is obtained from the Kac--Moody algebra by BRST
reduction (Definition~\ref{def:quantum-ds}):
$\mathcal{W}^k(\fg) = H^0(
\widehat{\fg}_k \otimes \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{gh}},\,
Q_{\mathrm{DS}})$.
We compose Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km} with the exactness
of DS reduction on the relevant filtered complexes.

\emph{Step~1: Functoriality of the bar construction under DS.}
The bar functor sends $\widehat{\fg}_k$ to
$\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\widehat{\fg}_k)$, and the DS differential
$Q_{\mathrm{DS}}$ acts on the bar complex (since $Q_{\mathrm{DS}}$
is a derivation of the vertex algebra structure; the bar construction
preserves this action as it is functorial for $A_\infty$ morphisms).
By the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:w-algebra-koszul-main}, Step~2,
the bar functor is exact on the homotopy category and:
\[
\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg))
\;\simeq\;
H^*_{Q_{\mathrm{DS}}}\!\bigl(
\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\widehat{\fg}_k)
\otimes \barB(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{gh}})\bigr).
\]

\emph{Step~2: DS reduction of the semi-infinite complex.}
On the semi-infinite side, DS reduction of
$C^{\infty/2+\bullet}(\widehat{\fg}_k, V_k)$ yields
$C^{\infty/2+\bullet}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg), M_k)$:
the semi-infinite complex of the W-algebra is the BRST
reduction of the semi-infinite complex of $\widehat{\fg}_k$.
This is the content of Feigin--Frenkel's construction of
W-algebra BRST cohomology~\cite{Feigin-Frenkel}: the
semi-infinite differential $Q_{\mathrm{si}}$ commutes with
$Q_{\mathrm{DS}}$ (both are BRST differentials for different
symmetries; their commutator vanishes by the standard double
complex argument).

\emph{Step~3: Comparison.}
The quasi-isomorphism $\Psi$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km} intertwines the
$Q_{\mathrm{DS}}$-action on both sides (since $\Psi$ is
constructed via the PBW spectral sequence, which respects the
adjoint action of $\widehat{\fg}_k$ on itself and hence the
DS differential).  Passing to $Q_{\mathrm{DS}}$-cohomology:
\[
H^*_{Q_{\mathrm{DS}}}(\Psi) \colon
H^*_{Q_{\mathrm{DS}}}(\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\widehat{\fg}_k)
\otimes \barB(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{gh}}))
\;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\;
H^*_{Q_{\mathrm{DS}}}(
C^{\infty/2+\bullet}(\widehat{\fg}_k, V_k)
\otimes C^*(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{gh}}))
\]
is a quasi-isomorphism (a quasi-isomorphism of filtered complexes
remains a quasi-isomorphism after applying an exact functor on the
derived category, which $H^*_{Q_{\mathrm{DS}}}$ is for
$k \neq -h^\vee$ by Arakawa's vanishing theorem
\cite{Ara15}).  The left side is
$\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg))$ (Step~1); the right
side is
$C^{\infty/2+\bullet}(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg), M_k)$ (Step~2).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Virasoro bar complex = semi-infinite complex;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{cor:virasoro-semi-infinite}
\index{semi-infinite cohomology!Virasoro}
\index{Virasoro algebra!semi-infinite cohomology}
For the Virasoro algebra $\mathrm{Vir}_c$ at central charge
$c = 1 - 6(k+1)^2/(k+2)$ \textup{(}obtained as
$\mathcal{W}^k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$\textup{)}:
\[
H^*(\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathrm{Vir}_c))
\;\cong\;
H^{\infty/2+*}(\mathrm{Vir}_c,\, M_c)
\]
where $M_c$ is the vacuum Virasoro module.  The Motzkin-number
bar cohomology dimensions of
Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:virasoro-chiral-koszul}} are therefore
semi-infinite cohomology dimensions.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w} with
$\fg = \mathfrak{sl}_2$, $f = f_{\mathrm{prin}}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Anomaly complementarity for \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{W}$}{W}-algebra pairs;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{cor:anomaly-duality-w}
\index{anomaly cancellation!W-algebra duality}
Let $\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)$ be the principal W-algebra, with
Feigin--Frenkel same-family partner
$\mathcal{W}^{k'}(\fg) = \mathcal{W}^{-k-2h^\vee}(\fg)$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The semi-infinite anomaly coefficients satisfy the same
level-independent complementarity law as the bar curvature
coefficients.  For principal finite-type $\mathcal{W}$-algebras,
\[
\kappa(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)) + \kappa(\mathcal{W}^{k'}(\fg))
= \bigl(c(\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)) + c(\mathcal{W}^{k'}(\fg))\bigr)
\varrho(\fg),
\]
where $\varrho(\fg) = \sum_{i=1}^r \frac{1}{m_i+1}$ is the anomaly
ratio from Theorem~\ref{thm:wn-obstruction}.  Thus the sum is a
level-independent constant: $13$ for Virasoro and $250/3$ for
$\mathcal{W}_3$.

\item The quantum complementarity theorem
\textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:quantum-complementarity-main})}
applied to the W-algebra Koszul pair
\textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:w-algebra-koszul-main})} gives:
\[
Q_g(\mathcal{W}^k) \oplus Q_g(\mathcal{W}^{-k-2h^\vee})
= H^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g,\, Z(\mathcal{W}^k)).
\]
Via the bar--semi-infinite identification, this is anomaly duality
for W-algebra pairs at all genera.

\item For $\fg = \mathfrak{sl}_2$
\textup{(}Virasoro\textup{)}: the Virasoro at
$c$ and its same-family shadow partner at $c' = 26 - c$ have
semi-infinite anomaly coefficients adding to~$13$, and their
genus-$g$ quantum corrections sum to
  $H^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g, Z(\mathrm{Vir}_c))$.  Here
  $\mathrm{Vir}_{26-c}$ is the proved M/S-level shadow partner used in
  the semi-infinite calculation; the stronger H-level
  infinite-generator realization belongs to MC4
  (Chapter~\ref{chap:concordance}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Combine Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w} with
Theorem~\ref{thm:wn-obstruction} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:central-charge-complementarity}: the DS reduction
preserves the anomaly data, and the principal finite-type
$\mathcal{W}$-obstruction is $\kappa = c\,\varrho(\fg)$.
Part~(b) then follows from the quantum complementarity theorem.
Part~(c): specialize to $\fg = \mathfrak{sl}_2$ with $h^\vee = 2$,
for which $c + c' = 26$ and $\varrho(\mathfrak{sl}_2)=1/2$.
\end{proof}

\section{The Chern--Simons structure in non-quadratic Koszul duality}

\subsection{Maurer--Cartan and Chern--Simons}

The Maurer--Cartan equation for non-quadratic chiral algebras:
\[
d\alpha + \frac{1}{2}\ell_2(\alpha, \alpha) + \frac{1}{6}\ell_3(\alpha, \alpha, \alpha) + \cdots = 0
\]
(using the $L_\infty$ brackets $\ell_n$ obtained by antisymmetrizing the $A_\infty$ operations)
is precisely the equation of motion for Chern--Simons theory with higher corrections.

\subsection{Witten's Chern--Simons interpretation}

Chern--Simons theory on a 3-manifold $M$ with gauge group $G$ at level $k$ produces~\cite{Wit89} the WZW model on $\partial M$ and quantum group representations at $q = e^{\pi i/(k+h^\vee)}$.  The action is:
\[
S_{CS}(A) = \frac{k}{4\pi} \int_M \text{Tr}\left(A \wedge dA + \frac{2}{3}A \wedge A \wedge A\right)
\]

\subsection{The precise connection}

\begin{theorem}[Chern--Simons equations from Koszul duality;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]\label{thm:cs-koszul-km}
\index{Chern--Simons!from Koszul duality}
For a simple Lie algebra $\fg$ and its affine extension
$\widehat{\fg}_k$ at $k \neq -h^\vee$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \emph{Classical Chern--Simons.}
  The Chevalley--Eilenberg complex $C^*(\fg)$ is the bar
  construction $\barB(U\fg)$\textup{;}
  the Maurer--Cartan equation in $C^*(\fg) \otimes \Omega^1(M)$
  for a $3$-manifold $M$:
  \[
  d\alpha + \tfrac{1}{2}[\alpha, \alpha] = 0
  \]
  is the flatness equation $F_A = 0$, which is the equation of
  motion for the Chern--Simons functional
  $S_{\mathrm{CS}}(A) = \frac{k}{4\pi}\int_M
  \mathrm{Tr}(A \wedge dA + \frac{2}{3}A^3)$.
\item \emph{Chiral Chern--Simons.}
  The bar--semi-infinite quasi-isomorphism
  \[
  \barB(\widehat{\fg}_k) \simeq
  C^*_{\infty/2}(\widehat{\fg}_k)
  \]
  (Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km})
  identifies the bar complex with the BRST complex of
  the WZW model at level~$k$, which is the gauge-fixed
  Chern--Simons theory on the boundary
  \textup{(}Witten~\cite{Wit89}\textup{)}.
  The MC equation in $\barB(\widehat{\fg}_k)$
  therefore parametrizes flat $\fg$-connections at
  level~$k$.
\item \emph{Curvature = CS level.}
  At genus~$1$, the bar complex has $\dfib^{\,2} = \kappa \cdot \omega_1$
  with $\kappa = k\dim(\fg)/(2(k+h^\vee))$.  This curvature is
  the Chern--Simons level: the bar complex is curved precisely
  when $k \neq 0$ \textup{(}nontrivial gauge theory\textup{)},
  and anomaly cancellation $\kappa + \kappa' = 0$ for the dual
  pair $(k, -k-2h^\vee)$ is the CS level-matching condition.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Part~(i) is classical: $C^*(\fg) = \barB(U\fg)$ by the
Chevalley--Eilenberg theorem, and the MC equation
$d\alpha + \frac{1}{2}[\alpha, \alpha] = 0$ in the dg~Lie algebra
$\fg \otimes \Omega^*(M)$ is the flatness equation $F_A = 0$ by
definition.  The flatness equation is the Euler--Lagrange equation
for $S_{\mathrm{CS}}$: varying $\delta S_{\mathrm{CS}}/\delta A
= \frac{k}{2\pi} F_A = 0$.

Part~(ii) chains three identifications:
(a)~$\barB(\widehat{\fg}_k) \simeq C^*_{\infty/2}(\widehat{\fg}_k)$
is Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km} (PBW filtration +
Arkhipov functor);
(b)~the semi-infinite complex of $\widehat{\fg}_k$ is the BRST
complex of the WZW model (Feigin--Frenkel, \cite{FF});
(c)~the WZW model on a surface $\Sigma$ is the boundary theory
of Chern--Simons on $M$ with $\partial M = \Sigma$
(Witten~\cite{Wit89}).
Composing, $\barB(\widehat{\fg}_k) \simeq C^*_{\mathrm{BRST}}
(\mathrm{CS}_k|_{\partial M})$, and MC elements in the bar complex
correspond to flat connections modulo gauge.

Part~(iii) follows from
$\dfib^{\,2} = \kappa \cdot \omega_1$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:genus-universality}) with
$\kappa(\widehat{\fg}_k) = k\dim(\fg)/(2(k+h^\vee))$
(Remark~\ref{rem:km-central-charge-sum}).  For the dual pair
$(k, k' = -k-2h^\vee)$,
$\kappa + \kappa' = 0$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:anomaly-duality-km}), which is precisely
the CS level-matching condition for the Feigin--Frenkel dual
theories.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texorpdfstring{$L_\infty$}{L-infinity} Maurer--Cartan as homotopy
flatness; \ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{thm:linf-mc-flatness}
\index{Chern--Simons!Koszul correspondence}
\index{L-infinity algebra@$L_\infty$ algebra!Maurer--Cartan}
For a chiral algebra $\cA$ with $A_\infty$ operations
$\{m_n\}$ \textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:w-algebra-ainfty}}
for W-algebras\textup{)}, the bar complex $\barB(\cA)$
carries an $L_\infty$ structure with brackets $\ell_n$
obtained by antisymmetrizing~$m_n$.  The Maurer--Cartan
equation
\[
d\alpha + \tfrac{1}{2}\ell_2(\alpha, \alpha)
+ \tfrac{1}{6}\ell_3(\alpha, \alpha, \alpha)
+ \cdots = 0
\]
is a \emph{homotopy flatness} equation: it defines the
formal moduli space of flat connections on the
``dual gauge theory'' associated to~$\cA^!$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For quadratic $\cA$
  \textup{(}Kac--Moody\textup{)}: $\ell_n = 0$ for
  $n \geq 3$, and the MC equation is the standard
  Chern--Simons flatness $dA + A \wedge A = 0$
  \textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km}(i))}.
\item For W-algebras obtained by DS reduction of
  $\widehat{\fg}_k$: the MC equation is the
  DS-reduced flatness equation, i.e., the generalized
  KdV hierarchy.
\item For general non-quadratic $\cA$: the higher
  $\ell_n$ give BV-BRST corrections to CS.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The $L_\infty$ structure on $\barB(\cA)$ is obtained
from the $A_\infty$ structure by the standard
antisymmetrization (Loday--Vallette \cite[Thm.~10.1.13]{LV12}):
$\ell_n(x_1, \ldots, x_n) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
\epsilon(\sigma)\, m_n(x_{\sigma(1)}, \ldots,
x_{\sigma(n)})$.  The MC equation
$\sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{1}{n!}\ell_n(\alpha^{\otimes n})
= 0$ is then automatic from the $A_\infty$
relations (which are equivalent to the $L_\infty$
Jacobi identities under antisymmetrization).

For~(i): when $\cA$ is quadratic (Kac--Moody), the
bar complex has $m_n = 0$ for $n \geq 3$
(the OPE has only simple and double poles), so
$\ell_n = 0$ for $n \geq 3$ and the MC equation
reduces to $d\alpha + \frac{1}{2}[\alpha, \alpha] = 0$,
which IS the CS equation of motion
(Theorem~\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km}).

For~(ii): the DS reduction functor
$H_{\mathrm{DS}}\colon \widehat{\fg}_k\text{-mod}
\to \mathcal{W}^k(\fg)\text{-mod}$ is exact on the
bar complex (Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w}).
Applying DS to the KM flatness equation
$dA + A \wedge A = 0$ gives the constrained flatness
$dA + A \wedge A = 0$ subject to the constraint
$A|_{\mathfrak{n}_+} = f$ (where $f$ is the nilpotent defining
the W-algebra).  This constrained flatness IS the
generalized KdV equation (Drinfeld--Sokolov \cite{DS}),
and the higher $\ell_n$ encode the constraint.

For~(iii): this is established in
Theorem~\ref{thm:cs-koszul-general} below.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[CS/Koszul for general non-quadratic
algebras; \ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{thm:cs-koszul-general}
For a general chiral algebra $\cA$ with Koszul dual $\cA^!$,
the Maurer--Cartan equation in the $L_\infty$ algebra
underlying the bar complex $\barB(\cA)$ takes the form of a
deformed Chern--Simons equation:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:deformed-cs-general}
d\alpha + \tfrac{1}{2}\ell_2(\alpha, \alpha)
+ \tfrac{1}{6}\ell_3(\alpha, \alpha, \alpha)
+ \cdots
= \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{1}{n!}\ell_n(\alpha^{\otimes n})
= 0.
\end{equation}
Specifically:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For quadratic $\cA$
  \textup{(}Kac--Moody\textup{)}: $\ell_n = 0$ for
  $n \geq 3$, and \eqref{eq:deformed-cs-general} reduces
  to the Chern--Simons flatness equation
  $d\alpha + \frac{1}{2}[\alpha, \alpha] = 0$
  \textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km}(i))}.
\item For non-quadratic $\cA$
  \textup{(}W-algebras, Yangians\textup{)}: the bar
  differential carries higher $A_\infty$ operations
  $m_n$ for $n \geq 3$
  \textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:bar-ainfty-complete}}\textup{)},
  yielding nonzero $\ell_n$ for $n \geq 3$.
  The MC equation~\eqref{eq:deformed-cs-general} is a
  homotopy flatness condition whose higher terms encode
  the non-quadratic OPE relations.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The argument proceeds in three steps.

\emph{Step~1: $A_\infty$ coalgebra structure on the bar complex.}
By Definition~\ref{def:bar-differential-complete}, the bar
complex $\barB(\cA) = T^c(s^{-1}\bar{\cA})$ carries a
codifferential $D$ encoding the chiral operations of~$\cA$.
When $\cA$ has non-quadratic OPE relations (e.g., W-algebras),
$D$ decomposes as $D = D_1 + D_2 + D_3 + \cdots$ where
$D_n$ is the component of tensor arity~$n$, yielding
$A_\infty$ co-operations $\Delta_n$ dual to operations~$m_n$.
The identity $D^2 = 0$ is equivalent to the $A_\infty$
relations among the~$m_n$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-ainfty-complete}).

\emph{Step~2: $A_\infty \to L_\infty$ by antisymmetrization.}
The standard $A_\infty$-to-$L_\infty$ correspondence
(Loday--Vallette \cite[Thm.~10.1.13]{LV12}) produces
$L_\infty$ brackets on $s^{-1}\bar{\cA}$ by
antisymmetrization:
\[
\ell_n(x_1, \ldots, x_n) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
\epsilon(\sigma)\, m_n(x_{\sigma(1)}, \ldots,
x_{\sigma(n)}).
\]
The $A_\infty$ relations for the $m_n$ translate,
under this antisymmetrization, into the higher Jacobi
identities for the~$\ell_n$.

\emph{Step~3: Maurer--Cartan equation.}
For any $L_\infty$ algebra $(\fg, \{\ell_n\})$, the
Maurer--Cartan equation is \emph{defined} as
\[
\mathrm{MC}(\alpha) \;:=\;
\sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{1}{n!}\,
\ell_n(\alpha, \ldots, \alpha) = 0,
\]
i.e., $\ell_1(\alpha) + \frac{1}{2}\ell_2(\alpha,\alpha)
+ \frac{1}{6}\ell_3(\alpha,\alpha,\alpha) + \cdots = 0$.
Writing $d = \ell_1$ (the linear part of the bar
differential), this is precisely
equation~\eqref{eq:deformed-cs-general}.  The higher
Jacobi identities for the $\ell_n$ guarantee that the
MC locus $\mathrm{MC}^{-1}(0)$ is well-defined and
controls the formal deformation theory of~$\cA$.

For~(i): when $\cA$ is quadratic, $m_n = 0$ for $n \geq 3$
(the OPE has only simple and double poles), so $\ell_n = 0$
for $n \geq 3$ and the MC equation reduces to
$d\alpha + \frac{1}{2}[\alpha, \alpha] = 0$,
which is the CS equation of motion
(Theorem~\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km}).

For~(ii): when $\cA$ is non-quadratic, the bar differential
has components of all arities (Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-ainfty-complete}),
giving nonzero $\ell_n$ for $n \geq 3$.
The resulting MC equation~\eqref{eq:deformed-cs-general} is
a homotopy flatness equation whose higher terms are determined
by the non-quadratic OPE data of~$\cA$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Physical interpretation]
\label{rem:cs-koszul-heuristic}
In the BV-BRST formalism, the higher $\ell_n$ for $n \geq 3$
correspond to higher-order interaction vertices in the
gauge-fixed action, with fields of mixed ghost degree so that
the total form degree remains~$3$ on a $3$-manifold.
For quadratic algebras we recover pure Chern--Simons; for
non-quadratic algebras, each higher OPE relation contributes
a higher-order vertex.  Identifying the $\ell_n$ with
\emph{specific} BV-BRST corrections to a Chern--Simons
action functional (in the sense of Costello--Gwilliam~\cite{CG17})
requires the perturbative QFT framework and is not addressed here.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Scope]
Theorem~\ref{thm:linf-mc-flatness} gives $L_\infty$ MC = homotopy flatness for all chiral algebras; Theorem~\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km} completes the CS/Koszul correspondence for KM (bar $\simeq$ semi-infinite $\simeq$ BRST $\simeq$ gauge-fixed CS); Theorem~\ref{thm:cs-koszul-general} gives the deformed flatness condition~\eqref{eq:deformed-cs-general} in general.  Identifying higher $\ell_n$ with BV-BRST action terms requires the Costello--Gwilliam framework~\cite{CG17}.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Open-string bar identification; \ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{thm:open-string-bar}
\index{open-closed correspondence!open sector}

a holomorphic-topological theory with boundary condition supporting
a Kac--Moody or W-algebra vertex algebra.  Then the bar complex
$\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{bdy}})$ computes the
open-string state space: there is a quasi-isomorphism
\[
\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{bdy}})
\simeq
C^{\frac{\infty}{2}+\bullet}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{bdy}})
\]
to the semi-infinite (BRST) complex of~$\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{bdy}}$.
Moreover, the bar-cobar adjunction of Part~I
\textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:verdier-bar-cobar})} realizes
the Verdier duality exchanging boundary and bulk data at the level
of chain complexes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For Kac--Moody boundary conditions
$\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{bdy}} = \widehat{\fg}_k$ ($k \neq -h^\vee$),
Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km} provides the quasi-isomorphism
$\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\widehat{\fg}_k) \simeq C^{\frac{\infty}{2}+\bullet}(\widehat{\fg}_k)$
via the PBW filtration and Arkhipov's functor.

$\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{bdy}} = \mathcal{W}_k(\fg)$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w} gives the analogous
identification through Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction.

formulation of the open-string BRST complex: its cohomology
computes the physical state space of open strings ending on
the holomorphic-topological boundary condition.

Theorem~\ref{thm:verdier-bar-cobar}, which establishes the
bar-cobar exchange as Verdier duality on Fulton--MacPherson
compactifications.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Modular anomaly for KM and \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{W}$}{W}-algebras;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]
\label{thm:modular-anomaly-km-w}
\index{modular anomaly!KM and W-algebras}
For a Kac--Moody algebra $\widehat{\fg}_k$ or W-algebra
$\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)$, the modular anomaly weight at
genus~$1$ equals $(c - c_{\mathrm{crit}})/24$, where
$c_{\mathrm{crit}} = 26$ \textup{(}bosonic\textup{)}
or $c_{\mathrm{crit}} = 15$ \textup{(}super\textup{)}.

Precisely: let $\cA$ be $\widehat{\fg}_k$ or
$\mathcal{W}^k(\fg)$ with central charge~$c$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The bar complex at genus~$1$ transforms under
  $\mathrm{SL}_2(\bZ)$ with weight $c/24$
  \textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:modular-invariance})}.
\item The bar complex computes BRST\slash semi-infinite
  cohomology:
  $H^*(\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA)) \cong
  H^*_{\mathrm{si}}(\cA)$
  \textup{(}Theorems~\textup{\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km}}
  and~\textup{\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w})}.
\item The anomaly coefficient satisfies $\kappa + \kappa' = 0$
  for Koszul dual pairs $(\cA, \cA^!)$
  \textup{(}Corollaries~\textup{\ref{cor:anomaly-duality-km}}
  and~\textup{\ref{cor:anomaly-duality-w})}.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, anomaly cancellation
$\kappa(\cA) = 0$ occurs if and only if $c = c_{\mathrm{crit}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine the three established results.
By~(i), the genus-$1$ bar complex transforms with
weight~$c/24$.  By~(ii), this complex IS the BRST
complex: $\barB^{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA) \cong
C^*_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\cA)$ as chain complexes
(the bar differential coincides with the semi-infinite
differential via the PBW filtration for KM or the
DS reduction for W-algebras).  By~(iii), the anomaly
coefficient $\kappa = c/(2(k+h^\vee))$ for
$\widehat{\fg}_k$ satisfies $\kappa + \kappa' = 0$
under $k \mapsto -k - 2h^\vee$.  The critical
central charge $c_{\mathrm{crit}} = 26$ appears as
the ghost contribution: the $bc$-ghost system at
weights $(2,-1)$ has $c_{\mathrm{gh}} = -26$, so total
anomaly cancellation requires
$c_{\mathrm{matter}} = 26$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Physical anomaly cancellation for KM and \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{W}$}{W}-algebras;
\ClaimStatusProvedHere]\label{thm:anomaly-physical-km-w}
\index{anomaly cancellation!KM/W-algebras}
For Kac--Moody algebras $\widehat{\fg}_k$ at $k\neq-h^\vee$ and W-algebras $\mathcal W^k(\fg)$ at non-critical level, impose all coefficient-action, specified square-zero target, filtration, actual symbol-map, and compatible-correction hypotheses of Theorems~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km} and~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w}.
On those supplied comparison carriers, the genus-zero assertions below have no additional string-central-charge condition:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The bar complex computes semi-infinite \textup{(}BRST\textup{)}
  cohomology:
  $H^*(\barB(\cA)) \cong H^{\infty/2+*}(\cA)$
  \textup{(}Theorems~\textup{\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km}}
  and~\textup{\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w})}.
\item The anomaly duality $\kappa + \kappa' = 0$ holds for
  Feigin--Frenkel dual pairs
  \textup{(}Corollaries~\textup{\ref{cor:anomaly-duality-km}}
  and~\textup{\ref{cor:anomaly-duality-w})}.
  This is anomaly cancellation: the matter-ghost system has
  $\kappa_{\mathrm{tot}} = 0$ precisely when
  $c = c_{\mathrm{crit}}$.
\item At genus~$0$, the Chern--Simons equations of motion
  are recovered from the Maurer--Cartan equation in the bar
  complex \textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km})}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Parts~(i) and~(ii) are restated from the cited theorems and
corollaries, which are proved using the PBW filtration,
Arkhipov functor, and Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence
(Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-km}) or the
Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction cascade
(Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-semi-infinite-w}).
Part~(iii) follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:cs-koszul-km}:
the bar--semi-infinite identification transports the MC equation
to the CS flatness equation via the WZW/CS boundary correspondence.
\end{proof}

The genus-$0$ identifications of
Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:anomaly-physical-km-w}} extend to all
genera: the BV-BRST identification
$\barB(\cA) \simeq C^{\mathrm{BRST}}(\cA)$ holds as a
quasi-isomorphism of \emph{genus-graded} complexes, so that the
quantum master equation
$\hbar \Delta S + \tfrac{1}{2}\{S, S\} = 0$ is the chain-level
refinement of $\Dg{g}^{\,2} = 0$ at every genus
\textup{(}Convention~\textup{\ref{conv:higher-genus-differentials})}.
